newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI reveals toolbox for future Euro central bank.
newsitem.headline: EMI reveals toolbox for future Euro central bank.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the European Central Bank, on Friday unveiled its planned policy toolkit aimed at ensuring strong credibility for Europe's monetary union from 1999.

In a report published in Frankfurt, the EMI unveiled a set of monetary policy instruments for the future central bank, but made clear that the final decisions on several key outstanding issues would have to be made by the ECB itself.
The new central bank will not be up and running until sometime next year. It assumes its monetary policy responsibility for Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the start of 1999.
The report shows that the new central bank will use central monetary policy instruments very close to those of the German Bundesbank.

It will offer funds to banks at two main rates which will set the floor and ceiling for money market rates, similar to the role performed by the Bundesbank's Lombard and discount rates. Open market operations will be its main policy tool.
The report left decision on the issue of exactly what form of policy strategy the ECB will adopt to the central bank, but recommended targeting either inflation or the money supply.

It also left open the question of whether the European Central Bank would use minimum reserves -- which require banks to deposit some funds at the central bank -- in its policy. The Bundesbank has pushed hard for the inclusion of this instrument.
